message.content:
I bought 44 shares of Apple (AAPL) at a limit of $223.00, which filled at $223.00 — a total of $9,812, comfortably inside the $10,000-per-order and $20,000-daily caps, with no money leaving the account (cash $50,000 → ~$40,188).

**What I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01), this morning's feed, the latest news, and the live quote before acting. The 10-K showed a business that is slowing at the top line but improving in quality of earnings: total net sales of **$391,035 million** (up 2% from $383,285 million), gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%, Services revenue up 13% to $96,169 million, and **operating income of $123,216 million** (up from $114,301 million) with **operating cash flow of $118,254 million**. Reported **net income of $93,736 million** and **diluted EPS of $6.08** were down year over year only because of the one-time, non-cash-operating **$10.2 billion** net State Aid tax charge tied to the ECJ's September 2024 ruling in the Ireland case — excluding it, profitability clearly improved. The offsetting negatives are real but not disqualifying: Greater China net sales fell 8% to $66,952 million, iPhone revenue was flat, and Wearables/Home/Accessories declined 7%. News confirmed the trajectory — Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, the strongest growth in several quarters — while feed headlines were neutral ("Apple shares little changed in early trade," "iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December," "Analysts keep holiday-quarter estimates unchanged"). I noted the intraday drift from ~$221.84 down to ~$220.53 in the morning feed, but the broker's latest quote was $222.70 last / $222.72 ask at 15:05Z, so I anchored my limit at $223.00 — about 0.13% above the ask, close enough to the market to fill without chasing. I sized to 44 shares (~$9.8k) rather than 45 so that even a full fill at the limit stays under the per-order cap, and I verified the $50,000 cash balance meant no transfer or margin was required.
